families.decision: 100% grass-fed, grass-finished beef, lamb or bison, AGA or PCO sealed; organic a bonus.
buying_tips: Look for the AGA, PCO 100% Grassfed or AWA seal: grass and forage through harvest.
Pick grass-finished over organic; organic beef can still be grain-finished.
Check the certifier’s name and website printed beside any grass-fed claim.
Pick a GAP-rated pack when no AGA seal is on the shelf; GAP bars feedlot finishing.

families.decision: USDA Organic poultry or pork with a Certified Humane, AWA or GAP pasture label.
buying_tips: Look for USDA Organic for organic feed and year-round outdoor access.
Pick a welfare seal: Certified Humane, Animal Welfare Approved or a high GAP step.
Read the name for ‘added solution’ or a retained-water percentage; pick neither.
Check the ingredient line for plain meat, or salt, named seasonings and a simple coating.

families.decision: USDA Organic pasture-raised eggs with a Certified Humane or AWA pasture seal.
buying_tips: Look for USDA Organic plus pasture-raised; organic alone is the floor.
Check for a Certified Humane, AWA or Real Organic seal beside ‘pasture-raised’.
Read ‘cage-free’ and ‘vegetarian fed’ as housing and feed words, not outdoor time.
Pick a refrigerated carton with clean, uncracked shells.

sources.name: Certified Humane cage-free vs free range

families.decision: USDA Organic or pasture-sealed meat, simply prepared, with a short ingredient list.
buying_tips: Look for the AGA Grassfed seal on beef products such as hot dogs, or USDA Organic.
Read every meat, fat and seasoning ingredient, including sauce sublists.
Skip nitrite, nitrate or celery curing, smoke flavor, MSG and unnamed oil blends.
Read for ‘mechanically separated’ meat in the ingredients and pick a pack without it.

families.decision: Organic bone broth, bones named first, with no yeast extract or flavor powder.
buying_tips: Look for the USDA Organic seal on the broth or soup.
Read the broth ingredients for bones and the animal species.
Pick short recipes of broth, meat, vegetables, herbs and salt.
Skip yeast extract, MSG, hydrolyzed protein and flavor powders in the ingredients.

families.decision: Wild-caught seafood, species and origin named, with the MSC label when sold.
buying_tips: Read wild-caught, the species and harvest origin on the label.
Look for the blue MSC label on wild fish; it marks an assessed fishery.
Read the ingredients: seafood alone, with optional salt.
Pick sealed frozen packs or firm fish displayed on ice.

families.decision: Wild trout when offered; otherwise US farmed rainbow trout, ASC-labeled if sold.
buying_tips: Look for wild-caught trout with harvest waters named.
Read ‘farm-raised’ and the country; pick rainbow trout farmed in the US.
Look for the ASC label on farmed trout packs.
Skip trout labeled color added.

families.decision: Crab or lobster, species and origin named, moving if live, plain if frozen.
buying_tips: Read the species and harvest origin on the tag.
Look for the MSC label on frozen or cooked crab and lobster.
Check live animals for moving legs or claws.
Read raw or cooked on chilled or frozen portions.

families.decision: Live clams, mussels or oysters with a harvest tag and intact shells.
buying_tips: Ask at the fish counter to see the harvest tag for loose shellfish.
Read the harvest waters and harvest date on the tag.
Check oysters, mussels and hard-shell clams for intact shells that close when tapped.
Pick farmed mussels or oysters as readily as wild; both rate Super Green.

families.decision: Dry or dry-packed scallops, with scallops as the only ingredient.
buying_tips: Read ‘dry’ or ‘dry-packed’ on the pack or the counter sign.
Read scallops as the only ingredient; skip added water or phosphates.
Ask at the fish counter whether the scallops are dry or wet-packed.
Pick sealed frozen dry scallops when the counter has only wet ones.

families.decision: Wild smoked fish or roe, species named, cured with salt and wood smoke.
buying_tips: Read the species, wild-caught wording and harvest origin.
Skip liquid smoke, smoke flavoring and added colors in the ingredients.
Check the curing method and storage directions on the label.
Pick intact packs kept chilled or frozen as their label directs.

aisles.decision: Pick the seal first, then read the cut, carton or ingredient list.
buying_tips: Look for AGA Grassfed on beef and lamb; USDA Organic plus a welfare seal on poultry.
Check egg cartons for pasture-raised with a Certified Humane or AWA seal.
Read the name for ‘added solution’, ‘tenderized’ or a retained-water percentage.
Read the certifier’s name and website beside any grass-fed or pasture claim.

aisles.decision: Read the full recipe first, then check how the case holds the food.
buying_tips: Read the full ingredient list, including seasoning, sauce and coating sublists.
Look for USDA Organic on prepared meats, salads and meals.
Skip celery or nitrite curing, smoke flavor and MSG in deli meats.
Check the case: hot food at 140°F or above, cold food at 40°F or below.

aisles.decision: Name the species, origin and wild or farmed, then use the matching seafood checks.
buying_tips: Read the species, wild or farm-raised, and country of origin on every label.
Look for MSC on wild seafood and ASC on farmed seafood.
Pick fish on a thick bed of ice that smells mild, not fishy or sour.
Check frozen packs for tears, frost or ice crystals before buying.

pick_steps: Read the country of origin first; it is printed by law.
Read the ingredients: shrimp, and salt at most.
Buy it frozen raw: the ‘fresh’ case is nearly always thawed.

beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed.decision: Grass-finished beef with an AGA or PCO 100% Grassfed seal.
beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed.delta: Grass-finished is a separate claim from grass-fed; read which one is printed.
beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed.short_answer: Look for the AGA or PCO Certified 100% Grassfed seal: grass and forage from weaning to harvest. Organic is a bonus, not the bar; organic beef can be grain-finished up to 120 days.
pick_steps: Read for an AGA or PCO seal or ‘grass-finished’; artwork is not a claim.
Without grass-finished, USDA Organic is next; organic beef can still be grain-finished.
At the counter, ask what it was finished on and whose definition.
Read the name for ‘mechanically tenderized’, ‘needle tenderized’ or ‘blade tenderized’.
Read the cut name: chuck and round work hardest; loin and rib work least.
Check the grade on the label: Prime, Choice and Select rate marbling only.

ground_beef_lean_ratio.decision: 100% grass-fed, grass-finished ground beef, beef only.
ground_beef_lean_ratio.delta: Lean/fat ratio is a separate printed number; ‘hamburger’ may include added beef fat.
ground_beef_lean_ratio.short_answer: Pick ground beef with beef as the only ingredient. The lean/fat ratio on the front is a separate number.
pick_steps: Look for an AGA or PCO seal; organic is a bonus.
Read the ingredients: beef only, nothing added.
Pick ‘ground beef’ over ‘hamburger’, which can include added beef fat.

pork_cuts_and_enhanced.decision: Pasture-raised pork first, then organic, no added solution.
pick_steps: Find the ‘% added solution’ figure and the solution’s listed ingredients.
Pick pork with Certified Humane, AWA or a GAP step on the pack.

lamb_goat.decision: Grass-fed lamb or goat first, then AGA or organic.
pick_steps: Look for USDA Organic: certified organic feed and outdoor access.
Pick lamb that is fine textured and firm, with white marbling.
Pick goat with firm, fine-grained flesh and well-distributed white fat.

organ_meats.decision: Grass-fed beef liver or heart first, then organic.
organ_meats.delta: Pick a single organ named as the cut, such as beef liver or heart.
pick_steps: Ask the meat counter which organs it stocks, fresh or frozen.
Look for an AGA seal on beef liver and heart; organic is a bonus.
Match each organ to its method; heart and tongue go in liquid.

butcher_counter_asking.delta: Ask what the beef was finished on, and for bones and trim.
pick_steps: Soup bones: ask the butcher for marrow or knuckle bones.
Ask for a whole chuck ground fresh to order.
Ask the butcher to portion it; cutting, tying and boning are usually included.
Read the ingredients: liver first, short list.
Check the fat is animal fat, not neutral oil.
Look for USDA Organic or a pasture seal on the pack.
Ask whether the calves were raised on pasture with their mothers.
Check the color: light red or pink, not white.
Look for USDA Organic or a welfare seal on the veal.

poultry_chicken_wings.decision: Pasture-raised chicken wings first, then organic; plain, uncoated.
poultry_chicken_wings.short_answer: Choose organic wings with a Certified Humane, AWA or GAP pasture label. Read the name for retained water or added solution, and skip breading or sauce.
pick_steps: Look for USDA Organic: certified organic feed and outdoor access.
Read the name for a retained-water or added-solution figure.
Pick plain wings without breading or sauce.

egg_labels.short_answer: Pick USDA Organic pasture-raised eggs with a Certified Humane or AWA seal. Certified Humane pasture-raised means 108 square feet per hen, outdoors daily. Cage-free and vegetarian-fed say nothing about time outdoors.
egg_labels.tier_note: Carton words alone are the producer’s own; a certifier’s pasture seal is audited.

label_cage_free.delta: Cage-free means uncaged hens, not outdoor access; free-range adds outdoor access of any size.
label_cage_free.short_answer: Cage-free means hens are not in cages; they can be kept indoors. Pick pasture-raised with a Certified Humane or AWA seal, then organic, then cage-free.
pick_steps: Read past ‘cage-free’; look for ‘pasture-raised’ with a certifier seal.
Next: pasture-raised organic, then organic, then cage-free.

label_pasture_raised_feed.decision: Certified Humane or AWA pasture-raised eggs, organic feed.
pick_steps: Pick pasture-raised eggs with a Certified Humane, AWA or Real Organic seal.
Next choose pasture-raised organic, then organic, then cage-free.
Read ‘vegetarian fed’ as feed only; it says nothing about pasture.

egg_duck_quail.decision: Pasture-raised duck or quail eggs first, then organic.
egg_duck_quail.short_answer: Pick duck or quail eggs labeled pasture-raised, organic where the case has them. Duck eggs are larger with bigger yolks. Quail eggs are tiny, about 10 to 12 grams each.

chicken_cuts_basics.decision: Pasture-raised whole chicken first, then organic with a welfare seal.
chicken_cuts_basics.delta: Whole bird first, then bone-in thighs; ‘no retained water’ on the pack.
pick_steps: Bone-in, skin-on thighs are the forgiving pick; boneless skinless costs the most.
Look for USDA Organic: certified organic feed and outdoor access.
Read for a retained-water percentage; ‘no retained water’ is the pick.
chicken_cuts_basics.cart_pick: Pasture-raised whole chicken or bone-in thighs

chicken_breast.decision: Pasture-raised breast first, then organic; bone-in and skin-on.

poultry_duck.decision: Pasture-raised whole duck with the skin on.
poultry_duck.short_answer: Choose a whole duck labeled pasture-raised or USDA Organic. Roasting a whole duck leaves extra fat to render and keep for cooking.
pick_steps: Look for pasture-raised or USDA Organic on the duck.
Pick a whole duck with the skin intact.
Save the rendered fat in a jar.

bison.decision: AGA Grassfed bison, with bison the only meat listed.

venison_game.decision: Plain venison cuts with the deer species named.

deli.decision: Organic pasture-raised whole-muscle deli meat, sliced at the counter.

seafood_trout.decision: Wild trout, or US farmed rainbow trout.
pick_steps: Ask the counter whether wild trout is in stock.
Without wild, pick US farmed rainbow trout.

farmed_fish_by_species.decision: Filter-feeding shellfish first; US rainbow trout for finfish.
